page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8559C cores running at 3.2 GHz. The processor includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The hardware configuration is completed by 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Local storage is a key feature of this instance, which includes a bundled 937 GB NVMe SSD. This local storage capacity, combined with the dedicated CPU allocation, makes the instance suitable for data-intensive workloads. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.34 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and memory read-only small block bandwidth categorized as weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage and strong single-core execution without the overhead of a GPU. The presence of hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA_NI) and integer manipulation flags supports secure data processing. This server is best suited for storage-heavy and database workloads, single-threaded data processing, and applications that benefit from high local SSD performance and moderate memory capacity.
